component.name: Apache Directory
component.description: Family of identity-infrastructure components: the ApacheDS LDAP v3 directory server, the LDAP API client/codec library, the Kerby Kerberos implementation (KDC plus token/PKINIT preauth), the Fortress RBAC/ARBAC authorization system (core, REST endpoint, web console, container realm), the SCIMple SCIM 2.0 provisioning implementation, the Mavibot MVCC B-tree storage engine, and the Studio desktop LDAP client. The umbrella threat model (DRAFT v0, not yet reviewed by the Directory PMC) captures the shared trust shape: a network service that authenticates a remote principal and then authorizes its requests over a wire protocol (LDAP, Kerberos, SCIM/HTTP, Fortress REST).

externalReferences.comment: Source security model document; this file is a structured translation of it.

blueprints.name: Directory identity stack
blueprints.description: Shared architecture described by the umbrella: server-side identity components exposing wire-protocol listeners to untrusted network clients, with the trust transition at authentication plus authorization, backed by operator-managed configuration, schema, ACIs, Kerberos realm/keytabs, RBAC policy, TLS material, and trusted backing storage.

assets.name: ApacheDS LDAP server
assets.description: LDAP v3 server (bind, search, modify, ACI), embedding Kerberos/DNS; host of the umbrella model. The BER/ASN.1 decoder is the first thing untrusted bytes hit; after a bind establishes identity (simple/SASL), ACIs authorize each operation.

assets.name: LDAP API codec
assets.description: LDAP protocol API and ASN.1/BER codec used on both client and server sides; parses untrusted LDAP PDUs in both directions.

assets.name: Kerby Kerberos KDC
assets.description: Kerberos KDC (AS/TGS), client, crypto, and PKINIT/token preauth. AS-REQ/TGS-REQ from any network peer reach the KDC; pre-authentication, ticket issuance, and encryption-type negotiation are the trust transitions; the KDC master key and per-principal keys are the crown jewels.

assets.name: Fortress RBAC stack
assets.description: RBAC/ARBAC policy engine over LDAP (fortress-core) plus the REST service (enmasse), web admin console (commander), and container security realm. Policy decisions are the boundary; the REST and web tiers add HTTP auth, CSRF, and injection surfaces.

assets.name: SCIMple SCIM 2.0 endpoint
assets.description: SCIM 2.0 provisioning implementation over HTTP/JSON; provisioning requests must be authenticated and authorized, and the filter/PATCH parsers are an injection/DoS surface.

assets.name: Mavibot MVCC storage engine
assets.description: MVCC B-tree storage backend. Its trust input is the on-disk B-tree and the records the trusted server layer hands it: corruption resistance and bounds, not a network boundary.

assets.name: Directory Studio desktop client
assets.description: Eclipse-based desktop LDAP client, modelled lightly as a client: its in-model surface is parsing untrusted responses from a directory it connects to, not serving requests.

zones.name: Network clients
zones.description: Peers speaking LDAP, Kerberos, SCIM/HTTP, or Fortress REST/HTTP before authenticating; untrusted. Authenticated principals are trusted up to their directory/RBAC permissions.

zones.name: Identity services
zones.description: The server-side components and their operator-managed configuration, schema, ACIs, Kerberos realm/keytabs, RBAC policy, and TLS material.

zones.name: Backing storage
zones.description: Data partitions (Mavibot or another backend), the policy LDAP for Fortress, and keytabs, on trusted disk protected at the filesystem layer.

persona.description: A peer speaking LDAP/Kerberos/HTTP before authenticating; untrusted. The primary adversary of the model.

Bound LDAP user, Kerberos principal, or authenticated SCIM/REST caller; trusted up to its directory/RBAC permissions. As an under-privileged principal attempting to exceed its ACIs or RBAC roles it is the secondary adversary.
A principal with directory-admin, Kerberos-admin, or Fortress-superuser rights; trusted, and an authorized admin action is not a finding.
Controls server config, schema, ACIs, the Kerberos realm and keytabs, the RBAC policy data, TLS material, and the backing store. Trusted; out of model as adversary.

assumptions.description: JVM services with operator-managed configuration, schema, ACIs, Kerberos realm/keytabs, RBAC policy, and TLS material; backing storage is on trusted disk.
Clocks are synchronized within the Kerberos skew window; TLS/StartTLS, SASL, and Kerberos crypto are available and operator-configured.

The stack binds protocol ports, reads/writes its data partitions and keytabs, performs crypto, and the Fortress tiers open HTTP listeners and bind to a backing LDAP; it is not assumed to execute host commands.

Cryptographic-primitive internals (the JCE provider) are out of scope except as the components select and use them; examples, samples, integration-test harnesses, and build tooling across all repos are out of scope.

threats.name: Authentication bypass at a listener
threats.description: A privileged operation performed without the bind, Kerberos preauth, or SCIM/REST authentication verifying the principal violates the shared authentication-integrity property. Critical severity.

threats.name: Authorization bypass or privilege escalation by an under-privileged principal
threats.description: An authenticated principal reads or modifies directory entries, Kerberos principals, or RBAC policy beyond its authorization, or escalates roles/permissions, including SoD/DSD policy bypass in RBAC. LDAP ACIs, Fortress RBAC/ARBAC, and SCIM authorization confine a principal to permitted operations; note the false friend that an RBAC role assignment is not active permission until the session activates the role.

threats.name: Parser crash or DoS from malformed wire-protocol input
threats.description: The LDAP BER codec, Kerberos ASN.1 parser, and SCIM JSON/filter parsers are expected to reject malformed or oversized input cleanly rather than crashing, hanging, reading out of bounds, or corrupting memory. Attack classes named: ASN.1/BER parser DoS, XXE/JSON-bomb in SCIM/REST, and search-filter complexity abuse.

threats.name: Kerberos ticket forgery, replay, or enctype downgrade
threats.description: Forged or replayed Kerberos tickets, downgrade to weak encryption types (RC4/DES) the realm still permits, Kerberoasting of weak service keys, and PKINIT/token-preauth edge cases. Tickets are bound to the issuing key and protected by timestamps and replay caches; weak enctypes are restrictable. The false friend: Kerberos 'encryption' of a ticket is integrity/authenticity, not a guarantee against a permitted weak enctype.

threats.name: CSRF, XSS, and injection in the Fortress and SCIM web tiers
threats.description: The Fortress REST endpoint and web console and the SCIM endpoint add HTTP surfaces: CSRF and XSS in the console, and injection payloads (LDAP filter, SCIM filter, SQL/LDAP injection via the management tiers).

threats.name: MITM or downgrade where transport protection was expected
threats.description: TLS/StartTLS and SASL provide confidentiality and integrity when configured; a MITM or downgrade where protection was expected violates the transport-security-support property. High severity.

threats.name: Storage inconsistency or corruption in Mavibot
threats.description: A reader seeing torn or inconsistent state, or corruption from concurrent writes or crash, would violate the storage-integrity property of Mavibot's MVCC design. Internal invariants not reachable from server-accepted input are out of the input surface.

threats.name: Hostile directory server responses parsed by Studio or the LDAP API client
threats.description: A malicious LDAP server versus a Studio or ldap-api client: the client components do not protect the user against a hostile server they chose to connect to beyond robust parsing. Findings requiring a malicious server the user connected to are low-priority client-side hardening, not server-side VALID findings.

threats.name: Operator misconfiguration and no-security-without-configuration exposures
threats.description: Pure misconfiguration is out of model: weak ACIs, an open anonymous bind left enabled, a Kerberos realm with weak crypto enabled, RBAC policy mistakes, TLS disabled, or an unauthenticated Fortress REST endpoint or console. Anonymous LDAP, weak enctypes, or an unauthenticated REST/console expose the service to the extent the operator left them open; whether the insecure posture is a shipped default is an open wave-1 maintainer question. The operator, and anyone holding the KDC master key, admin DN, Fortress superuser, keytabs, or filesystem access, is out of model as adversary.

threats.name: LDAP/SCIM filter injection in a downstream application
threats.description: An LDAP search filter is a query language, not inert data: filter injection via unsanitized input concatenated by a downstream application is the LDAP analogue of SQL injection, but it is that application's bug, not a server bug.

trustBoundaries.name: Wire-protocol trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: The shared boundary is the wire-protocol request before authentication and authorization complete. A finding is in-model on a server inbound path if reachable from an unauthenticated or under-privileged remote principal before the component's auth/authorization gate; a finding requiring admin rights or a misconfiguration is out of model.

trustBoundaries.name: Backing storage trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: Mavibot consumes data from the trusted server layer; backing storage (data partitions, policy LDAP, keytabs) sits on trusted disk protected at the filesystem layer by the operator.

controls.name: Authenticate principals before privileged operations
controls.description: LDAP bind (simple/SASL), Kerberos pre-authentication, and SCIM/REST authentication verify the principal before privileged operations across the stack.

controls.name: Authorization enforcement (ACIs, RBAC/ARBAC, SCIM authz)
controls.description: LDAP ACIs, Fortress RBAC/ARBAC decisions (including role activation and SoD/DSD constraints), and SCIM authorization confine each principal to permitted operations.

controls.name: Robust protocol parsing
controls.description: The LDAP BER codec, Kerberos ASN.1 parser, and SCIM JSON/filter parsers reject malformed or oversized input cleanly rather than crashing or corrupting memory (the model records the hardening bounds as an open maintainer question).

controls.name: Enforce TLS/StartTLS and SASL protection
controls.description: Enforce TLS/StartTLS (and SASL confidentiality/integrity) on all protocols; transport protection is operator-configured.

controls.name: LDAP operator hardening
controls.description: Disable anonymous/unauthenticated access unless intended, set restrictive ACIs and admin limits, enforce TLS/StartTLS, and bound search-filter complexity and result sizes.

controls.name: Kerberos operator hardening
controls.description: Disable weak enctypes (RC4/DES), require preauth, protect the KDC master key and keytabs, keep clocks synced, and keep the replay cache on.

controls.name: Fortress operator hardening
controls.description: Authenticate and TLS-protect the REST endpoint and web console, protect the policy LDAP, and configure SoD/DSD constraints deliberately.

controls.name: SCIM operator hardening
controls.description: Require authentication and authorization on every SCIM endpoint, and bound filter, PATCH, and JSON sizes.

controls.name: Protect storage at the filesystem layer
controls.description: Protect the data partitions and keytabs at the filesystem layer, and back up.

controls.name: Track advisories and stay on supported lines
controls.description: Track ASF advisories and stay on supported release lines.
